headline: Understanding Scleral Lens Replacement: When and Why

blocks.text: Scleral lenses generally have an expected lifespan of one to two years, though some lenses may last longer. The expected lifespan of an individual's scleral lenses can vary based on factors such as the lens brand, material, and personal circumstances. There is no fixed replacement deadline for every patient.

Several factors can lead to the need for scleral lens replacement. These include the accumulation of deposits, damage such as surface cracking or breakage, or changes in the lens fit or prescription power.

The surfaces of gas-permeable scleral lenses can deteriorate due to repeated wearing and handling. Careful handling can help preserve the lens surface, but re-polishing a lens is not always a viable option.
If a scleral lens needs replacement, the new lens may not be an identical copy. The existing design might be duplicated, adjusted, or a new fitting may be required.
It is recommended to inform an eye-care provider about any changes in lens fit or vision, lenses that repeatedly shift, or lenses that become difficult to remove.

brief.audience: Patients considering or using scleral lenses for keratoconus
brief.goal: Answer the audience concern about needing to replace scleral lenses over time: explain supported reasons for replacement and whether there is one deadline for everyone. Encourage patients to visit the eye clinic for individual advice.

reviewed_title: Understanding Scleral Lens Replacement: When and Why
editor_notes: Answer the replacement question directly. Attribute the general one-to-two-year lifespan to Cleveland Clinic and keep it together with the qualifications that some lenses last longer and timing depends on the individual. Explain deposits, surface wear, damage and changed fit or prescription. Tell readers to contact their eye-care provider about changes in fit or vision, shifting lenses or difficulty removing them. Do not give a universal deadline or imply Nexus offers specific services. No em dashes. Keep explanations concise and avoid claims about improved outcomes or guaranteed comfort.
